items.summary: Raise KStack runtime maturity from Advanced to Master
items.description: Coordinate the Jira-first runtime program across release, Host, Domain, Memory, secret lifecycle, and measured provider qualification without transferring evidence between lanes.

items.summary: Stage KStack improvement review after primary readiness
items.description: Change material design and process-improvement review so one ordered primary agent iterates alone to a clean confidence of at least 93 before the other agent receives the neutral current design for independent final review; permit Codex or Claude Opus in either role and return final-review findings to the primary without every-round dual dispatch.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC01 canonical host schemas
items.description: Implement the frozen HP-TC01 normative schemas and canonicalization contract with closed-schema and adversarial fixtures.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC02 trusted host request context
items.description: Implement trusted request context and deterministic host-operation class derivation from the closed HP-TC02 design.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC03 replay and authoritative time
items.description: Implement idempotency, replay refusal, and authoritative-time handling with restart and clock-adversary tests.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC04 live host evidence selection
items.description: Implement protected live measurement, evidence trust, and deterministic host-capability selection using the repaired HP-TC04 chain.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC05 host eligibility and quarantine
items.description: Implement deterministic eligibility, quarantine, and fail-closed UNKNOWN outcomes without granting authority from capability evidence.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC06 independent host harness
items.description: Implement the independent conformance harness and complete bypass inventory so every effect boundary is proven or reported UNKNOWN.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC07 structural host broker
items.description: Implement the frozen structural broker requirement and preserve the protected host-governance boundary on every supported host.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC08 race-resistant host mutation
items.description: Implement restart-closed, race-resistant local mutation with durable terminal outcomes and cleanup-boundary crash tests.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC09 MCP principal boundary
items.description: Implement the MCP principal and output boundary while preserving the digest-frozen public registry and prohibiting private-data promotion.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC10 host receipt trust
items.description: Implement operation-class receipt trust, query-only reconciliation, and ambiguity-preserving retry refusal.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC11 host leases and activation
items.description: Implement leases, exact host binding, activation fencing, in-flight rules, and fresh reverse-activation lineage.

items.summary: Implement HP-TC12 reversible host rollout
items.description: Implement reversible migrations and rollout seams with backward readability or verified restore and forward recovery.

items.summary: Implement HB-TC01 canonical host packages
items.description: Implement canonical Agent Skills packages, typed declarative host profiles, semantic tool and path rendering, bundles, clauses, resolver, provenance, and typed installer handoff without literal replace-all translation.

items.summary: Implement HB-TC02 transactional host installer
items.description: Implement the generic transactional installer with clean install, upgrade, rollback, and health contracts.

items.summary: Implement HB-TC03 OpenCode package and discovery
items.description: Implement the instruction-only OpenCode candidate package and discovery path without overstating host enforcement.

items.summary: Implement HB-TC04 read-only MCP facade
items.description: Implement the unauthenticated public read-only MCP tools and resources facade with no identity or authority promotion.

items.summary: Execute HB-TC05 OpenCode conformance
items.description: Run the frozen OpenCode conformance plan on a real installation and retain the scoped clean-install, invocation, and health evidence. Update, rollback, and persisted-data recovery evidence are not established by HB-TC05 and remain exclusively tracked by linux-lifecycle-qualification.

items.summary: Execute HB-TC06 second-host abstraction proof
items.description: Prove the shared host abstraction after OpenCode stabilizes and open Goose only as a separately qualified later host.

items.summary: Qualify Hermes as an optional KStack host
items.description: Package and qualify KStack Agent Skills and bounded MCP integration on Hermes without granting Hermes memory, tools, or subprocesses direct secret-value access.

items.summary: Qualify OpenClaw native and delegated KStack modes
items.description: Implement and qualify a minimal native analysis surface plus an authority-bound ACP execution bridge with capability selection, immutable work envelopes, content-free receipts, reconciliation, and no prompt-only authority.

items.summary: Qualify Goose as the independent second KStack host
items.description: Create a dedicated Goose objective and adapter, admit one exact signed and advisory-reviewed native release, execute the same stable profile through isolated protected conformance with distinct evidence, and only then complete the HB-TC06 abstraction proof without reusing OpenCode evidence.

items.summary: Qualify the KStack Linux distribution matrix
items.description: Qualify native-filesystem installs on approved Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora-family targets plus WSL2, recording kernel, filesystem, init, and package-manager differences.

items.summary: Qualify Linux cgroup pidfd and eBPF backends
items.description: Exercise privileged cgroup v2, pidfd, and eBPF paths on target kernels with real capability sets and explicit seam-tested versus qualified results.

items.summary: Prove Linux install upgrade rollback lifecycle
items.description: Repeat clean install, host discovery, invocation, upgrade, rollback, health, and persisted-data recovery on native Linux and WSL2 native storage.

items.summary: Implement the D0 closed domain-pack catalog
items.description: Implement the closed declarative catalog, host-neutral analysis-pack representation, safe native rendering, and independent pack lifecycle without redesigning the locked Option C architecture or granting rendered methods execution authority.

items.summary: Implement D1 authenticated domain-pack identity
items.description: Implement authenticated identity for selection, policy weakening, waiver, and activation with exact action binding and replay protection.

items.summary: Implement D2-F1 exact domain inventory
items.description: Implement exact-byte catalog inventory equality and stale-catalog refusal from the frozen D2-F1 design.

items.summary: Implement D2-F2 domain policy binding
items.description: Implement exact selection-policy binding so policy or catalog drift invalidates the decision before dispatch.

items.summary: Implement D2-F3 domain selection digest
items.description: Implement the closed selection digest and deterministic record consumed by domain-pack composition.

items.summary: Implement D3 domain separation of duty
items.description: Implement exact-target quorum and no-bypass separation for downgrade, policy weakening, and quarantine decisions.

items.summary: Implement D4 and D10 domain evidence handshake
items.description: Implement the pure result validator and workflow-owned authenticated evidence descriptor without giving the validator mutation authority.

items.summary: Implement D5-F1 domain schemas and digests
items.description: Implement closed pack, fixture, content, and evidence schemas with exact digest domains and undeclared-field rejection.

items.summary: Implement D5-F2 atomic pack activation
items.description: Implement atomic catalog and compatibility activation with historical-replay resistance and isolated rollback.

items.summary: Implement D6 deterministic domain budgets
items.description: Implement whole-request prompt accounting, catalog-owned applicability, stable overflow refusal, and deterministic composition caps.

items.summary: Implement D7 blinded domain evaluation
items.description: Implement fixed-power blinded evaluation with safety inference, human adjudication, baseline regression checks, and preserved gridlock.

items.summary: Implement D8 trusted domain freshness time
items.description: Implement authenticated time quorum, conservative freshness predicates, and external rollback witnesses.

items.summary: Ship and qualify the release-operations pack
items.description: Implement the first analysis-only domain pack and pass the blinded incremental-value corpus before any broader activation.

items.summary: Ship and qualify the product-experience pack
items.description: Implement product-experience as an independently reviewed reasoning and evidence pack without duplicating the executable experience gate.

items.summary: Ship and qualify the assurance pack
items.description: Design, implement, evaluate, activate, and independently roll back the assurance domain pack after its own closure.

items.summary: Ship and qualify the research-knowledge pack
items.description: Design, implement, evaluate, activate, and independently roll back the research-knowledge domain pack after its own closure.

items.summary: Qualify offline domain-content acquisition
items.description: Implement the exact-digest license-allowlisted seven-file assurance trial for offline translation only; prohibit direct runtime marketplace loading.

items.summary: Promote and install the product-experience candidate
items.description: Review the working tree, commit the exact candidate, reinstall the active KStack runtime, and prove clean install, upgrade, and health without claiming live qualification.

items.summary: Close PX-TC10 on an authorized staging target
items.description: Run all eight product-experience lanes and post-deploy v2 on synthetic authorized staging data with exact release, baseline, and Jira receipts.

items.summary: Close JT-TC01 Jira roadmap lifecycle
items.description: Complete adversarial coverage for roadmap preview, create or adopt, exact read-back, and ambiguous-result reconciliation.

items.summary: Independently close JT-TC03 Jira mapping
items.description: Review and close issue mapping, exact create or adopt, drift detection, ambiguous-response recovery, and ongoing new-item projection.

items.summary: Close JT-TC04 Jira comments and status
items.description: Add pagination, duplicate, ambiguity, and transition adversarial fixtures, then close marker-bound comments and portable status projection.

items.summary: Close JT-TC05 Jira release versions
items.description: Close release assignment, upgrade history, version administration boundaries, additive updates, and exact read-back.

items.summary: Close JT-TC06 Jira workflow wiring
items.description: Complete main-window aggregate status and independently close two-lane tracking across init, design, implementation, QC, review, Jira, and configuration.

items.summary: Close JT-TC07 live integrated Jira gate
items.description: After JT-TC01 through JT-TC06 close, execute migration, live KStack population, packaging, rollback, and the final integrated gate.

items.summary: Prove repeated deployment failure and rollback
items.description: Carry linked Jira work through authorized staging deployment, success validation, controlled failure, automatic rollback, restored-target validation, and a second operator or repository repeat.

items.summary: Implement Memory Slice 1 authority and citations
items.description: Implement the frozen authority and citation envelope while keeping Git and Jira authoritative and local Memory derived.

items.summary: Implement Memory Slice 2 exact and BM25 retrieval
items.description: Implement deterministic exact and BM25 retrieval, bounded cache behavior, and reproducible fixtures with no local model or embeddings.

items.summary: Implement Memory Slice 3 GitHub and Jira ingestion
items.description: Implement bounded GitHub and Jira ingestion, reconciliation, provenance, deletion behavior, and source-authority preservation.

items.summary: Implement Memory Slice 4 encryption and deletion
items.description: Implement encryption, key lifecycle, deletion tombstones, non-resurrection, crash recovery, and OS-specific durability tests.

items.summary: Implement Memory Slice 5 portable synchronization
items.description: Implement audit-chained sync, compaction, conflict handling, and portable Git objects without force push or silent conflict resolution.

items.summary: Close ECR TC05 transactional secret store
items.description: Finish the remaining TC05 groups and close the transactional encrypted-store design without granting runtime secret-use authority.

items.summary: Design and close ECR TC07 opaque handles
items.description: Define provider-neutral opaque handles, target binding, policy lookup, approval binding, and non-forgeable content-free receipts.

items.summary: Design and close ECR TC08 custody adapters
items.description: Define one developer OS-custody backend and one production secret-manager or workload-identity backend with no plaintext model return.

items.summary: Design and close ECR TC09 secret lifecycle
items.description: Define rotation, revocation, expiry, deletion, recovery, and non-resurrection semantics across every selected custody backend.

items.summary: Design and close ECR TC10 secret executor
items.description: Define the target-bound executor, bootstrap custody, output-leak rejection, crash behavior, and content-free operational evidence.

items.summary: Implement and qualify ECR TC11 secret workflow
items.description: Implement the selected opaque-handle path and pass synthetic retrieval, use, rotation, revocation, expiry, deletion, crash, and output-leak trials before production secrets.

items.summary: Qualify OpenClaw as an optional secret provider
items.description: Evaluate and qualify an exact pinned OpenClaw trusted-prompt, SecretRef, allowed-host, and egress-substitution cell behind the provider-neutral KStack broker without enabling file-backed, environment, arbitrary-command, or direct-value fallback paths.

items.summary: Run the Host KCRP provider A B trial
items.description: Create a canonical redacted Host packet and compare full versus reduced Codex runs for required findings, decisions, tokens, latency, cost, and mandatory-record preservation.

items.summary: Run the Domain KCRP provider A B trial
items.description: Create a canonical redacted Domain packet and compare full versus reduced Codex runs without activating a default reduction route.

items.summary: Run the Release Jira KCRP provider A B trial
items.description: Create a canonical redacted Release and Jira packet and measure full versus reduced provider behavior with equal required findings and decisions.

items.summary: Qualify one default-off KCRP provider route
items.description: Admit one route only after all packet trials preserve quality and mandatory evidence with exact provider tokens, latency, cost, and an empty credential-content surface.
